issues.description: Field Farm.animals: the problem statement is internally inconsistent and also inconsistent with the reference implementation. The UML diagram in problem_statement.md declares Farm.animals as List<Animal> (problem_statement.md line 17), the textual Part 3 instructions in problem_statement.md explicitly require the aggregation to be a Set implemented with a HashSet (problem_statement.md lines 108-111), but the provided reference implementation declares the field as a List and initializes it with an ArrayList (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 9-13). The template Farm.java also does not provide the collection and contains a TODO placeholder (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java lines 3-6). This contradiction (List vs Set/HashSet) leaves students unsure whether to implement uniqueness semantics and which collection type the autograder/tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: follow the textual instruction that requires uniqueness and change the reference solution and the template to use a Set<Animal> backed by a HashSet. Concretely, in both template and solution: change the field to 'private Set<Animal> animals;', add imports 'java.util.Set' and 'java.util.HashSet', initialize 'this.animals = new HashSet<>()' in the no-arg constructor, and update getter/setter signatures to use Set<Animal>. Alternatively, if List semantics were intended, update the problem statement (both the UML and the textual description) to request a List/ArrayList and remove references to HashSet/uniqueness. Ensure tests and instructions reflect the chosen design.
